characters.main: A young adult in their early twenties with messy brown hair, wearing a simple casual hoodie.
characters.dad: A middle-aged man with short grey-streaked hair and wire-rimmed glasses, wearing a knitted sweater.
characters.mom: A middle-aged woman with a messy hair bun, wearing comfortable oversized pajamas or a cozy cardigan.

scenes.narration: Okay, so... it’s like 1 AM, but I was thinking about this earlier and now I can't stop thinking about it.
scenes.visual: main sitting up in bed in a dark bedroom at night, staring wide-eyed at a glowing digital bedside clock reading 1:00 AM.

scenes.narration: At some point between when you're like twelve and twenty-two, your brain just... glitches.
scenes.visual: A humorous visual of a glowing brain floating in mid-air with cartoon pixelation glitches and a red loading bar appearing over it.

scenes.narration: You’re sitting in the passenger seat, watching your dad try to figure out how to connect his phone to the car Bluetooth, and this overwhelming realization hits you.
scenes.visual: Inside a car, main looks sideways with a sudden wide-eyed realization at dad, who is furiously poking a glowing car touchscreen menu.

scenes.narration: He’s not this all-knowing architect of reality.
scenes.visual: dad dressed as a giant glowing cosmic architect standing among blue grid lines, holding mini planets, floating above stars.

scenes.narration: He’s literally just a guy named Steve who is getting actively defeated by a dashboard menu and is winging basically everything.
scenes.visual: dad looking confused and overwhelmed, holding a smartphone next to a bright car dashboard displaying a huge warning symbol.

scenes.narration: Because think about when you were five.
scenes.visual: A tiny five-year-old version of main standing on a lawn, looking up with huge starry eyes of adoration.

scenes.narration: Your parents aren't even people to you back then.
scenes.visual: Five-year-old main looking up at dad and mom, who appear as tall glowing silhouettes towering into the sky.

scenes.narration: They're like... mythical creatures.
scenes.visual: dad and mom depicted as majestic mythological heroes with glowing capes standing atop a grassy hill.

scenes.narration: They know where the spare lightbulbs are kept.
scenes.visual: dad opening a glowing, treasure-chest-like cabinet in a dark garage, pulling out a sparkling lightbulb effortlessly.

scenes.narration: They deal with wasps.
scenes.visual: dad bravely standing on a porch step, calmly holding a glass jar to catch a cartoon buzzing wasp.

scenes.narration: They carry money in a wallet and they never seem to get lost or cry or sit in their driveway wondering if they picked the wrong major.
scenes.visual: dad driving a car down a sunny open highway, smiling confidently while holding a thick leather wallet.

scenes.narration: They're just environmental facts.
scenes.visual: A simple nature scene featuring mountains, clouds, and gigantic stone statues of mom and dad carved into the cliff side.

scenes.narration: Like gravity, or the roof.
scenes.visual: main standing safely under a house roof while an apple falls from a tree nearby.

scenes.narration: And then you get older, and the cracks start showing.
scenes.visual: A grand marble statue of dad sitting in a chair, with glowing white hairline cracks spreading across its surface.

scenes.narration: Maybe you walk into the kitchen at midnight and catch your mom standing in front of the open fridge, staring blankly into the cold light, eating shredded cheddar straight out of the bag.
scenes.visual: mom standing in a dark kitchen, illuminated only by the bright cold light of an open fridge, eating shredded cheese directly from a plastic bag.

scenes.narration: Or you hear your dad tell a casual story about his twenties and you realize... wait, he was a total menace who barely survived his own terrible choices?
scenes.visual: A young 1980s version of dad riding a skateboard off a wooden ramp while yelling wildly.

scenes.narration: Or even worse—you watch them react to bad news, and instead of some calm, infinite adult wisdom, you see the exact same quiet, spiraling anxiety that you get when a teacher asks you a question you didn't prepare for.
scenes.visual: dad and mom sitting together at a table, looking wide-eyed and anxious at a piece of paper, with sweat drops appearing above their heads.

scenes.narration: I actually looked this up down a rabbithole earlier—psychologists call it "parental de-idealization."
scenes.visual: main falling headfirst down a surreal circular tunnel surrounded by floating textbooks and floating question marks.

scenes.narration: Which sounds like a fake academic phrase, but it’s basically the moment you pull back the curtain in *The Wizard of Oz* and realize the terrifying, powerful ruler of the kingdom is just an anxious middle-aged dude sweating behind a panel.
scenes.visual: A large red velvet curtain pulled back to reveal dad sweating nervously while operating a wooden machine full of dials.

scenes.narration: Except in real life, the wizard is your dad, and the panel is a tax document he’s been procrastinating on for three weeks.
scenes.visual: dad sitting at a small desk piled high with messy tax papers marked with big red exclamation points, biting his nail nervously.

scenes.narration: And if you do the math, it’s even wilder.
scenes.visual: main pointing at a green chalkboard covered in simple equations connecting birth years and ages.

scenes.narration: When you were born, your parents were probably in their twenties or early thirties.
scenes.visual: A young version of mom and dad in retro clothing staring in shock at a tiny wrapped baby in a hospital room.

scenes.narration: Look at anyone who's twenty-four right now.
scenes.visual: A young adult in a messy room wearing mismatched socks, looking utterly bewildered.

scenes.narration: They are a disaster zone.
scenes.visual: A room with clothes scattered everywhere, a smoke alarm on the wall, and a clock spinning wildly.

scenes.narration: They eat cereal out of mug because all the dishes are dirty, lose their keys three times a day, and rely on pure vibes to pay rent on time.
scenes.visual: A young adult sitting on a couch eating colorful cereal from a coffee mug, surrounded by a tower of unwashed dirty dishes.

scenes.narration: Your parents were *those exact people*.
scenes.visual: Side-by-side comparison of young mom and young dad looking chaotic in the 1990s next to a modern stressed youth.

scenes.narration: They didn't get summoned from some ancient order of wise elders.
scenes.visual: A comical scene of ancient wise robes hanging on a rack, with young dad walking past them in jeans and a graphic t-shirt.

scenes.narration: They were literally just two random young adults who got handed a screaming baby and went, "Oh... cool. Guess we're doing this now."
scenes.visual: Young mom and dad standing together holding a screaming baby, both exchanging nervous, clueless expressions.

scenes.narration: Every rule, every grounded weekend, every confident explanation about why the sky is blue—they were freestyling.
scenes.visual: dad standing at a podium making theatrical hand gestures while secretly reading a hastily handwritten note behind his back.

scenes.narration: Making it up on the spot.
scenes.visual: mom nervously juggling three spinning plates labeled 'Dinner', 'Bedtime', and 'Homework'.

scenes.narration: And once you notice it, you can't unsee it.
scenes.visual: main wearing oversized magnifying glasses, peering forward with a surprised expression.

scenes.narration: You start seeing their weird habits not as "parent traits," but as human flaws.
scenes.visual: dad tripping awkwardly over his own shoelaces while carrying a basket of laundry.

scenes.narration: You notice your mom is genuinely insecure about her cooking.
scenes.visual: mom biting her lip anxiously as she looks at a slightly misshapen baked pie on a kitchen counter.

scenes.narration: You notice your dad gets angry because he’s actually just overwhelmed and doesn't know what else to do.
scenes.visual: dad holding a tangled giant ball of colorful string, looking completely stressed and baffled.

scenes.narration: You realize they have high school stuff they never got over, bad habits they can't break, and weird dreams they quietly gave up so you could have a bedroom with carpet.
scenes.visual: A dusty electric guitar sitting in an attic corner next to a brightly lit, cozy child's bedroom.

scenes.narration: And honestly, it kind of sucks at first.
scenes.visual: main sitting alone on a park bench looking down at the ground under a small grey rain cloud.

scenes.narration: Because when you stop seeing them as superheroes, you lose that safety net.
scenes.visual: A superhero cape floating away into the sky over an empty open field.

scenes.narration: You realize no one is secretly steering the ship.
scenes.visual: A wooden ship's steering wheel spinning on its own on an empty ship deck.

scenes.narration: There is no shadow committee of adults who have it all figured out.
scenes.visual: An empty dark boardroom table with empty chairs and cartoon smoke popping away.

scenes.narration: It’s just eight billion people pretending they know what’s going on while trying not to spill coffee on themselves.
scenes.visual: A crowd of diverse people walking in different directions, carefully balancing sloshing coffee cups.

scenes.narration: But... I don't know, it’s also kind of nice?
scenes.visual: main smiling softly as a bright sunbeam breaks through parted clouds in a outdoor setting.

scenes.narration: Because once you stop expecting them to be perfect, you can actually like... meet them.
scenes.visual: main standing eye-to-eye with mom and dad, all three sharing warm, relaxed smiles.

scenes.narration: As actual people.
scenes.visual: main and dad sitting together on a sunny park bench, casually talking like old friends.

scenes.narration: You stop asking "why did my parents ruin my life?" and you start going, "man, what kind of chaotic mess were they dealing with when they were my age?"
scenes.visual: main holding an old framed photo of young mom smiling next to a broken appliance.

scenes.narration: It turns it from this weird hierarchy into a real relationship.
scenes.visual: A tall steep pedestal crumbling away, leaving main, mom, and dad standing together on equal flat ground.

scenes.narration: You’re not just living in their kingdom anymore.
scenes.visual: A tiny cardboard castle wall falling down to reveal a warm, normal family living room behind it.

scenes.narration: You’re just two adults standing in the same room, both mildly confused by the universe, both trying to figure out how to make dinner without burning the kitchen down.
scenes.visual: main and dad standing side by side in a kitchen wearing aprons, staring quizzically at a smoking skillet.

scenes.narration: So next time your mom is struggling to open a PDF, or your dad is staring blankly at a shelf in the hardware store... just give them a break.
scenes.visual: dad staring blankly at a wall of identical screws in a hardware store aisle, while main puts a friendly hand on his shoulder.

scenes.narration: They’re doing a live playthrough of life with no tutorial, exactly like you.
scenes.visual: main and dad walking down a sidewalk together with glowing pixel video game text above them reading 'NO TUTORIAL'.
